newsitem.title: DUBAI: Inchcape in $12 mln UAE distribution centre.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape in $12 mln UAE distribution centre.

text.p: British conglomerate Inchcape Plc said it has invested $12 million in a distribution centre at Dubai's Jebel Ali Free Zone, al-Khaleej newspaper reported on Sunday.
"The regional distribution centre built at the cost of $12 million will start operations next month," the daily quoted regional executive director Philip Coshing as saying.
Coshing said the new distribution centre would serve Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Syria and Cyprus.

He said the group's sales in the Middle East grew 4.5 percent last year to 238.6 million pounds sterling ($397 million) from 228.3 million sterling in 1995. Operating profits grew 8.8 percent to 17.3 million pounds sterling.

Inchcape represents many of the world's best known consumer products' manufacturers. It specialises in the distribution of motor vehicles, soft drinks, consumer and industrial products, and office automation equipment, while its shipping service is the largest independent shipping network in the world.
